contract: Sources are validated against active sending SDP MID/kind; labels and stream IDs are not authority.
ontrack is staged until successful remote-description acceptance. Exact call/auth/peer callbacks fence publication.
Legacy selects the first active sending audio MID in SDP order; additional audio is quarantined. Protocol1 cannot silently downgrade.
Serialized offer/answer flow uses UUID/revision and exact pending-offer relation, polite rollback and impolite glare rejection.
Screen capture readiness requires a matching protocol1 remote answer for the exact sender/source/raw track and actual sending currentDirection, current capability and bounded owner predicate.
remoteStream is video only; microphone and screen audio have independent stream fields.

Explicit screenAudioRequested is accepted only for the active authenticated owner with confirmed peer capability before picker/share. Browser audio uses that same picker; native capture uses the isolated helper.

One audio session belongs to the exact call/auth generation/peer/video ticket/result/helper instance; audio stays disabled until exact source acknowledgement. Audio failure does not stop screen video.

Full pending-capture scope and audio-only scope are separate: capability/request loss retires raw audio while video may continue. Cancelled-video restoration uses exact independent call/peer/no-new-share authority and latest camera.
Rendered stopScreenAudio actions are bound to their original video ticket and helper instance. Retired actions cannot stop later shares or reauthenticated calls.
isScreenSharePending disables choice during picker and camera restoration. Camera-off metadata cannot clear a screen source; ended display metadata unregisters before asynchronous camera restoration.
remaining: Real two-client P2P browser/Windows SDP negotiation, simultaneous independent microphone/system-audio playback, glare and output-device acceptance remain open.
Generated group-call decoder evidence from earlier QA is not acceptance of this new P2P source protocol.
Native system-audio permissions, capture-device changes and physical output/deafen leakage require actual device acceptance.
No production deployment or release acceptance claimed.
